examGuide.title: Mental model and derivation
examGuide.body:
Disk scheduling examples usually model a rotating disk with seek cost proportional to cylinder movement. FCFS follows arrival order; SSTF picks the nearest request; SCAN continues to an endpoint before reversing, whereas LOOK reverses at the last pending request. Starting direction and whether endpoint travel is charged materially change totals. SSDs have different physical costs, so do not transfer seek-cylinder reasoning blindly.

**Key relationship:** Total head movement = sum of absolute differences between consecutive visited positions

examGuide.title: A repeatable solving procedure
examGuide.body:
1. Record head position and initial direction.
2. Apply endpoint versus last-request policy.
3. Sum absolute moves, not signed displacement.

examGuide.title: Approach the exam question
examGuide.body: Convert RPM to revolution time using 60/RPM seconds; average rotational latency is half a revolution. Add seek, rotational wait and actual transfer, using the access model given. Random sectors may each incur rotational wait; contiguous transfers often amortize it. Disk scheduling head movement is not the same as elapsed service time.

examGuide.title: Worked problem
examGuide.body:
A disk rotates at 12000 RPM and has 1000 sectors per track. What is transfer time for one sector in microseconds, ignoring seek and latency?

**Answer: 5.** A revolution takes 60/12000=0.005 s=5000 μs. At 1000 sectors per track, one sector passes in 5000/1000=5 μs.

examGuide.title: Conditions and edge cases
examGuide.body:
An average rotational delay of 2500 μs would be added only if requested. Do not confuse that waiting delay with the 5 μs sector-transfer time.

SCAN and LOOK can produce different totals because SCAN may travel to the disk endpoint.

examGuide.title: Worked question patterns
examGuide.body:
#### Pattern 1 · MCQ

LOOK differs from SCAN by:

- **A.** Reversing at the last pending request rather than disk endpoint
- **B.** Always using FCFS
- **C.** Ignoring direction
- **D.** Serving no requests

**Answer: A.** LOOK avoids unnecessary travel to an endpoint when no request lies farther in that direction.

#### Pattern 2 · MSQ

Choose true statements.

- **A.** FCFS uses request arrival order
- **B.** SSTF chooses a nearest pending cylinder
- **C.** Absolute movement equals signed displacement always
- **D.** Initial direction matters for SCAN

**Answer: A, B, D.** A reversal adds travel even if net displacement is small, refuting C.

#### Pattern 3 · NAT

Head starts at 50 and FCFS serves 10,70,30. Total cylinder movement?



**Answer: 140.** Moves are |50−10|=40, |10−70|=60 and |70−30|=40. Sum=140.

examGuide.title: Work through the supplied PYQs
examGuide.body:
#### GATE 2024 CS2 · Q53 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/io-scheduling?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** I/O and disk scheduling. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. At 6000 RPM, one revolution takes 60/6000=0.01 s=10 ms; average rotational latency is 5 ms.
2. A sector transfer takes 10/500=0.02 ms. With random locations, each sector costs about 5 ms seek+5 ms latency+0.02 ms transfer=10.02 ms.
3. For 3000 sectors this is 30060 ms=**30.06 s**, within the official accepted interval. Contiguous-track streaming would require a different access model.

#### GATE 2026 CS1 · Q59 · NAT

[Open the original question and try it](/#/lesson/io-scheduling?tab=practice)

**What is tested:** I/O and disk scheduling. Refer to the original image for complete givens and diagrams.

1. Seek distances in the prescribed order are 0→5:5 tracks, 5→12:7, 12→7:5, totaling 17 ms.
2. At 15000 RPM, a rotation takes 4 ms and average rotational latency is 2 ms. Thirty random sectors add 30×2=60 ms. Each sector transfers in 4/400=0.01 ms, adding 0.3 ms.
3. Total=17+60+0.3=**77.3 ms**.
